grant-call-center.name: Adam Grant's university call center study
grant-call-center.outcome: After callers met one scholarship student, they spent 142% more time on the phone and raised 171% more money a month later, using the same script
grant-call-center.limits: One university fundraising call center, reported through magazine coverage of Grant's work; figures differ across write-ups. A critic noted employers could use this to make up for low pay or demeaning work.
grant-call-center.locator: "were spending 142 percent more time on the phone"

hospital-cleaners.name: Wrzesniewski and Dutton's hospital cleaners study
hospital-cleaners.place: A hospital (location not given in the source read)
hospital-cleaners.outcome: Cleaners with the same tasks differed in how they saw the job; those who liked it saw themselves as part of healing patients and did extra things for them
hospital-cleaners.limits: Interview study at one hospital, read here through CNN's 2021 summary rather than the original paper, which does not say where the hospital was; shows a link, not that reframing causes satisfaction.
hospital-cleaners.locator: "playing a critical role in healing patients"

job-crafting-forms.name: Job crafting: task, relational and cognitive
job-crafting-forms.outcome: Term coined by Amy Wrzesniewski and Jane E. Dutton in 2001; defines three ways people reshape their own jobs: changing tasks, changing who they work with, and changing how they see the work
job-crafting-forms.limits: Encyclopedia summary; it lists individual studies but no meta-analysis, and notes crafting that suits the employee can clash with the employer's goals.
job-crafting-forms.locator: Intro: "coined by Amy Wrzesniewski and Jane E. Dutton in 2001"; section on the three forms

radiology-photos.name: Patient photos attached to CT scans
radiology-photos.outcome: With a patient's photo in the file, radiologists wrote more thorough reports; about 80% of incidental findings were missed when the photo was removed
radiology-photos.limits: A conference presentation with 318 patients and 15 radiologists at one hospital; the authors asked for larger studies.
radiology-photos.locator: "approaching the patient as a human being"

yougov-meaningless-2024.name: YouGov survey on meaningless jobs
yougov-meaningless-2024.outcome: 33% of 5,889 working Britons said their job is not making a meaningful contribution, down from 37% in 2015; 53% in retail and finance
yougov-meaningless-2024.limits: British, self-reported; a feeling about contribution, not a measure of what the work actually does.
yougov-meaningless-2024.locator: "is not making a meaningful contribution to the world"

soffia-useless-jobs.name: Soffia and colleagues' 2022 study of useless jobs
soffia-useless-jobs.outcome: Few and fewer workers felt their jobs were useless; the feeling tracked bad management and lack of control more than job type, and some essential workers such as garbage collectors felt it
soffia-useless-jobs.limits: Read through the Wikipedia article on Graeber's book, not the paper itself; a 2023 U.S. study by Walo found partial support for Graeber instead.
soffia-useless-jobs.locator: Criticism section; "the empirical data do not support any of Graeber's hypotheses"

chca-bronx.name: Cooperative Home Care Associates
chca-bronx.outcome: Home health aides own and run the agency, elect most of its board, and number more than 2,000 members; the average U.S. worker co-op has about nine; holds "Payday Fridays" when the otherwise isolated aides gather as a group, and president and CEO Adria Powell calls home care very isolating
chca-bronx.limits: Article is several years old and does not give wages; one unusually large co-op, not the typical case.
chca-bronx.locator: "Payday Fridays"; "Home care is very isolating" (Adria Powell)

mondragon.name: Mondragon cooperatives
mondragon.outcome: Nearly 70,000 worker-owners vote in general assemblies; the gap between highest- and lowest-paid employees is capped at a ratio of 6 to 1
mondragon.limits: Grew from one region's particular history; its first co-op, Fagor, is now defunct, and other sources give the pay cap as 9 to 1. The article's comparison figure for the United States links to a report on chief executive pay, a different measure.

uk-employee-ownership-trust.name: UK employee ownership trust law
uk-employee-ownership-trust.outcome: Owners who sell a controlling stake to a trust for employees pay no capital gains tax; staff bonuses up to £3,600 a year are free of income tax
uk-employee-ownership-trust.limits: A tax break for sellers, which some see as generous; the page gives no current count of trusts. Ownership through a trust does not guarantee workers a real say.
uk-employee-ownership-trust.locator: "was recognised in UK tax law in 2014"

nceo-esops.name: U.S. employee stock ownership plans
nceo-esops.outcome: 6,609 plans with about 15.1 million participants, roughly 11 million of them active
nceo-esops.limits: Most employee stock plans give workers a share of value, not a vote on how the company is run.

project-equity.name: Project Equity
project-equity.outcome: Nonprofit that helps owners sell their businesses to employees, including feasibility checks, financing and preparing workers for ownership; works with the field on federal, state and local employee ownership policy and keeps an interactive database of past and current state policy
project-equity.limits: The productivity and profit figures on its site are its own summary of others' research.
project-equity.locator: "Half of U.S. businesses with employees are owned by baby boomers"; /impact/public-policy/: "federal, state and local policies"

worker-coop-directory.name: U.S. Federation of Worker Cooperatives and Democracy at Work Institute directory
worker-coop-directory.outcome: A public directory of worker co-ops, other democratic workplaces and support groups
worker-coop-directory.limits: The page did not say how many co-ops are listed or what filters exist.
worker-coop-directory.locator: "The directory offers a compilation of the fast-growing community of worker coops."

taproot-pro-bono-value.name: Taproot Foundation pro bono valuation
taproot-pro-bono-value.outcome: Professional skills given to nonprofits valued at $150 an hour, against about $23 for general volunteering
taproot-pro-bono-value.limits: Taproot's own estimate, based on salary data, from 2015.
taproot-pro-bono-value.locator: "$150 per hour value of pro bono service"

catchafire.name: Catchafire
catchafire.outcome: Matches professionals with short nonprofit projects that use their work skills; founder Rachael Chong started it after hauling lumber when her finance skills could have helped
catchafire.limits: The page gives no numbers; many nonprofits get access through a funder, so listings vary by area.
catchafire.locator: "We're matching what people do in their day-to-day lives."

idealist-volunteering.name: Idealist volunteer listings (now including VolunteerMatch)
idealist-volunteering.outcome: More than 100,000 virtual and in-person volunteer opportunities, searchable by skill, such as data analyst or board member
idealist-volunteering.limits: A listing site; quality of each opportunity depends on the nonprofit.

repair-cafe.name: Repair Café
repair-cafe.outcome: Started by Martine Postma in 2009; volunteers with repair skills fix neighbors' things at more than 2,500 Repair Cafés worldwide
repair-cafe.limits: Count is the foundation's own; most cafés meet monthly or less.

80000-hours-guide.name: 80,000 Hours career guide
80000-hours-guide.outcome: Free, research-based guide to choosing work you're good at that also helps others, including ways to do good without changing jobs
80000-hours-guide.limits: Comes from the effective altruism movement and ranks causes by its own view of impact, which not everyone shares.
80000-hours-guide.locator: Guide home page; 15 parts plus appendix

onet-online.name: O*NET OnLine
onet-online.outcome: Free public database of occupations, with more than 19,000 task statements, work activities, work context and an interest profiler
onet-online.limits: Describes typical jobs, not your particular workplace.
onet-online.locator: "detailed descriptions of the world of work"

americorps.name: AmeriCorps
americorps.outcome: Federal service programs with a living allowance; full-time members can earn an education award of up to $6,095, and AmeriCorps Seniors is for people 55 and older; created by the National and Community Service Trust Act of 1993
americorps.limits: Full-time living allowances are modest, and programs and openings vary by state and year.
americorps.locator: Intro: "created by the National and Community Service Trust Act of 1993"; Benefits section; education award up to $6,095

encore-fellowships.name: Encore Fellowships (CoGenerate)
encore-fellowships.outcome: Places experienced professionals in nonprofits for about 1,000 paid hours over a year; more than 2,000 fellows to date
encore-fellowships.limits: CoGenerate and Encore pages blocked access in this run; figures seen only in search snippets. Hosts pay the stipend, and matching can take months.
